title: Introduce invocation deja-vu index and alert replay gateway
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: We frequently see noisy, one-off token-cost/latency incidents that are hard to reproduce and tune alerts for. Ops needs a compact, privacy-safe snapshot that can be replayed (in a sandboxed path) to validate alert thresholds, fallback policies, and model routing behavior. This PR implements a reproducible invocation fingerprint (the 'Deja-Vu Index') and an Alert Replay Gateway to drive deterministic replays of sampled invocations through the serving stack.

What this PR adds (high level):
- a Deja-Vu Index generator that computes a stable fingerprint for an invocation using prompt-shape hash, token-phase histogram, model variant, KV-cache hit profile, and lightweight kernel-queue signature; designed to be stable across minimal tokenization/whitespace differences
- a compact Invocation Snapshot format (sanitized, pseudonymous) that stores the Deja-Vu ID, truncated prompts, token shape metrics, KV cache markers, and a replay hint bundle
- an Alert Replay Gateway service (internal only) that can accept a snapshot and execute a deterministic replay path through a dedicated canary runtime with replay-only tracing hooks
- three Grafana dashboards: DejaVu Explorer, Alert Replay Runs, and Replayed SLO Deltas
- metric and span tags: invocation.deja_vu_id, alert_replay.run_id, replay.trace_phase
- a sampled-log compactor that keeps a delimited, privacy-safe excerpt for each snapshot for human triage
- migration that registers the new metric names and adds a lightweight retention TTL for snapshots.

Why it's safe: Snapshots are sanitized: full user PII is redacted, embeddings are not stored, and prompt payloads are truncated and hashed. The replay path is constrained to dedicated canaries and does not feed outputs back into production logs or billing pipelines. Access to replay snapshots gated by RBAC and audit-logged.

Checklist:
- [x] Deja-Vu Index algorithm and unit tests
- [x] Snapshot format + encoder/decoder
- [x] Replay gateway prototype + integration tests (uses canary runtime)
- [x] Dashboards and example alert-run (example run attached)
- [x] CI: unit/integration/e2e (replay e2e runs in sandbox)
- [x] Docs: docs/observability/deja-vu-replay.md
- [x] Migration: metrics registration and retention TTL

Notes & follow-ups:
- Performance: index computation adds ~120us median overhead per invocation in the fast path; we sample 0.5% by default. We can move to async sidecar if overhead becomes problematic.
- This PR intentionally avoids storing full prompt text; product requested hashed + truncated payloads to allow meaningful triage without exposing PII.
- Next steps: add a replay-run A/B harness to automatically attempt replays for high-confidence SLO regressions and surface suggested alert threshold edits.

review_comments: Jonas Patel: Nice approach. Two asks: (1) can we add a deterministic seed in the index so replays are bit-identical where possible? (2) please confirm storage TTL and deletion path for snapshots so compliance can sign off.
Maya Chen: Reply to Jonas - added deterministic seed (falls back to zero if unavailable) and added migration + admin API to purge snapshots older than TTL. Updated docs with retention and RBAC notes.

Evelyn Ruiz: Integration tests look good. Found one flaky test on macOS CI (test_replay_gateway::test_replay_path) — looks like a timing assert. Suggest switching to event-driven sync in test harness.
Maya Chen: Fixed test to wait on replay-run-complete event instead of a fixed sleep. Re-ran CI; e2e passed.
Marco Alvarez: Approving from SRE after verifying canary isolation and no billing side-effects. Small nit: add a metrics tag for 'replay.sandbox' true/false.
release_notes: Adds Deja-Vu invocation fingerprinting and an internal Alert Replay Gateway for reproducing and tuning alert behavior. New dashboards (DejaVu Explorer, Alert Replay Runs) and metrics (invocation.deja_vu_id, alert_replay.run_id) shipped. Snapshots are pseudonymous and retention is configurable.
